provider_query: CPython source file that defines PyObject_Malloc
answer:
**`PyObject_Malloc` is defined in `Objects/obmalloc.c`.**

On current CPython `main`, the public function is the object-domain allocator entry point (size check, stats, then `_PyObject.malloc`). The underlying pymalloc/mimalloc implementations live in the same file.

Relevant sources:

1. **Definition (current main)** — `Objects/obmalloc.c`  
   https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/main/Objects/obmalloc.c  
   Contains `void * PyObject_Malloc(size_t size)` under “the object allocator,” dispatching via `_PyObject.malloc`.

2. **Same file, older snapshot (3.7-era shape)** — function body shown as a thin wrapper over `_PyObject.malloc` after a `PY_SSIZE_T_MAX` check.  
   https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/3.7/Objects/obmalloc.c

3. **Historical direct pymalloc implementation** — older `obmalloc.c` defined `PyObject_Malloc` inline (pool/block path, `#undef PyObject_Malloc`).  
   https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/7aace7a2dc40562ecb7d59b49925948411e9d171/Objects/obmalloc.c

4. **Docs (API, not the definition)** — `Doc/c-api/memory.rst` documents `PyObject_Malloc` and the default object allocator (pymalloc, or mimalloc in free-threaded builds).  
   https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/main/Doc/c-api/memory.rst

5. **Related docs** — `Doc/c-api/allocation.rst` notes `PyObject_New` calls `PyObject_Malloc`; lists soft-deprecated `PyObject_MALLOC`.  
   https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/main/Doc/c-api/allocation.rst

6. **Domain declaration (header)** — `Include/pymem.h` associates `PyObject_Malloc` / `Realloc` / `Free` with `PYMEM_DOMAIN_OBJ` (declaration/API, not the body).  
   https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/d8f0d922d53a8f7bb64c1fda26be386bd2e3d958/Include/pymem.h

7. **Callers** — `Objects/object.c` uses `PyObject_Malloc` from `_PyObject_New` / `_PyObject_NewVar` (not the definition).  
   https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/55fee9cf216abe4ec0d1139f94b1930fbd0c7644/Objects/object.c

8. **File history** — commit history for `Objects/obmalloc.c` (pymalloc, debug hooks, per-interpreter state, free-threading/mimalloc).  
   https://github.com/python/cpython/commits/main/Objects/obmalloc.c

# memory layout

[Permalink: memory layout](https://github.com/zpoint/CPython-Internals/blob/master/Interpreter/pyobject/pyobject.md#memory-layout)

This is the layout of **PyObject**. It's the basic part of every other Python object

Every object in Python can be cast to **PyObject**, e.g., list, tuple, etc.

`PyObject_HEAD_EXTRA` is the head of the double linked list, it's used for keeping track in [Garbage Collection](https://github.com/zpoint/CPython-Internals/blob/master/Interpreter/gc/gc.md)

`ob_refcnt` stores reference count of the current object, it's also used in [Garbage Collection](https://github.com/zpoint/CPython-Internals/blob/master/Interpreter/gc/gc.md)

`ob_type` is a pointer to its type object. For example, `type("abc") ===> str`, `"abc"` is the PyObject, and `ob_type` in the PyObject will point to `str`

[![PyObject](https://github.com/zpoint/CPython-Internals/raw/master/Interpreter/pyobject/PyObject.png)](https://github.com/zpoint/CPython-Internals/blob/master/Interpreter/pyobject/PyObject.png)

# overview

[Permalink: overview](https://github.com/zpoint/CPython-Internals/blob/master/Interpreter/pyobject/pyobject.md#overview)

Whenever you execute a Python program from a `.py` file, the compile phase will translate the human-readable source code to a form called Python bytecode

The `pyc` file will be generated if necessary, and the interpreter phase will start the main loop, executing the bytecode in the `pyc` file line by line

The compiled `pyc` file will not boost the runtime of the program. Instead, the load time of the program will be faster because it doesn't need to generate the `pyc` file again

According to [PEP 3147](https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-3147/), after Python 3.3, `pyc` files will only be generated through the `import` mechanism, and `pyc` files will exist under the `__pycache__` directory

[![executePy](https://github.com/zpoint/CPython-Internals/raw/master/Interpreter/pyobject/executePy.png)](https://github.com/zpoint/CPython-Internals/blob/master/Interpreter/pyobject/executePy.png)

# ceval

[Permalink: ceval](https://github.com/zpoint/CPython-Internals/blob/master/Interpreter/pyobject/pyobject.md#ceval)

The main loop of the interpreter is defined in `cpython/Python/ceval.c`

```
main_loop:
    for (;;) {
    	// jump to fast_next_opcode if necessary
    	// check for signal hndler/async io handler
        // drop gil if needed
		fast_next_opcode:
            switch (opcode) {
                /* ... */
            }
    }
```
